subject: Capacity allocation & ramp plan for AtlasHealth Dedicated sizing
messages:
From: Charlotte Ross <charlotte.ross@atlashealth.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Oct 2027 16:23:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity request — AtlasHealth onboarding (SOW attached)

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're ready to move forward with the dedicated deployment for our clinical inference workload. Procurement asked me to share our initial sizing and timeline so we can align on resource commitments. High level:
- Target launch window: mid-Oct -> full onboarding by Nov 15
- Steady-state needs: ~8 A100-class GPUs (24/7) for model serving (mixed 2K-4K seqs)
- Ramp plan: start with a 4-GPU pilot for 2 weeks, then step to 8 once integration tests complete

Can Redwood prioritize this deal for us? Our CEO has tied this go-live to a vendor announcement and we need a predictable capacity path. I've attached the SOW (SOW_v1.pdf) and the procurement contact is Charlotte Ross (CC'd Sales Ops for billing).

What are next steps to lock provisional capacity while legal finalizes the contract? Any temporary burst options to get us through the pilot ramp?

Best,
Charlotte Ross
Head of Procurement, AtlasHealth
charlotte.ross@atlashealth.ai

I'll follow up with a proposed provisional plan by COB Monday.

Cheers,

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: AtlasHealth — options and constraints

Team — quick recap after looking at the SOW and our fleet telemetry:
- Atlas requests 8xA100 steady-state for Nov. Our current committed reserved pool for that region has ~14 A100 equivalents free across committed deals; however ~6 are already earmarked as "soft-reserve" for two large renewals in the same window.
- Risk: if both renewals draw on soft-reserve, we won’t be able to guarantee 8 unshared GPUs to Atlas by Nov 1 without re-prioritization.

Options to propose:
1) Staged reservation (preferred): allocate 4 dedicated A100 now (pilot), provide access to a preemptible burst pool (up to +4) for onboarding spikes. Convert to 8 dedicated post-contract effective date.
2) Dedicated tranche with preemption guards: provision 8 but allow soft-preemption outside SLO window (cheaper for customer, riskier reliability).
3) Marketplace brokerage: use CloudBroker for short-term capacity rental for up to 4 GPUs for the Oct-Nov ramp; higher cost but avoids changing current commitments.

Numbers & quick calc: baseline monthly token cost delta for option (1) vs option (3) is ~18% higher for (3) on token spend but avoids touching other deals.

Ask: Rishi, can you quantify SLO delta if we keep Atlas on 4 permanently until the other renewals clear (i.e., queueing vs latency percentiles)? Ben, do you have customer tolerance for burst-based onboarding (thing they accept short-term throttle or do they need guaranteed latency during pilot)?

If we can't resolve, we should escalate to product ops/leadership for reassigning soft-reserve (this would be an exception).

- Karthik

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, AtlasHealth Sales Ops <salesops@atlashealth.ai>
Date: Tue, 26 Oct 2027 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed provisional capacity & ramp — AtlasHealth

Charlotte —

Thanks for the patience. After reviewing options with the operations team, here's a practical approach that balances predictability and the current fleet constraints:

Proposed plan (provisional):
- Immediate (pilot): 4 dedicated A100-equivalent GPUs reserved starting Nov 1 for a 2-week pilot.
- Burst pool: access to a preemptible burst pool (up to +4 A100-equivalent) during the onboarding window (Nov 1 — Nov 15) to cover integration spikes. Burst will be best-effort and preemptible by higher-priority SLAs.
- Convert to full 8 dedicated GPUs no earlier than contract effective date (we'll commit to a conversion window within 7 business days of the effective date).
- Pricing: provisional-pricing.xlsx attached with a breakout for pilot vs burst vs full dedicated.

Next steps we need from you to finalize provisional reservation:
1) Formal signoff on the pilot and burst approach from procurement (reply to this thread).
2) Sample request traces or QPS estimate (tokens/request) in our shared Drive link.
3) Target effective contract date (tentative) so we can schedule permanent tranche conversion.

Notes/constraints: burst access is not SLA-backed and may have up to 2x median latency variance during preemption events. If Atlas requires strict latency guarantees during the onboarding ramp, we'll need to either (a) shift soft-reserve from lower-priority deals (leadership signoff) or (b) accept a brokerage add-on via CloudBroker (higher cost).

If this plan looks reasonable please reply with procurement thumbs-up and I'll create the provisional reservation ticket.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Sales (Dedicated) | Redwood Inference
vanessa@redwood.com

Attachments: provisional-pricing.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Charlotte Ross <charlotte.ross@atlashealth.ai>

Cc: AtlasHealth Sales Ops <salesops@atlashealth.ai>, CloudBroker Inc. <capacity@cloudbroker.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2027 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed provisional capacity & ramp — AtlasHealth

Vanessa —

Thanks, that approach is reasonable and better than we expected. Procurement gives provisional signoff for the pilot + burst path so you can proceed with the reservation ticket. A couple notes from our side:
- We will need an SLA exception during the two-week pilot where occasional latency blips are acceptable, provided you notify us of preemption windows.
- If it's possible to tier the burst so critical traffic (inference for hospital partners) gets priority inside our burst allocation, that would be hugely valuable.
- We'll push contract effective date to Nov 20 to give our legal team time; please confirm conversion window aligns with that.

Charlotte Ross
Head of Procurement, AtlasHealth
charlotte.ross@atlashealth.ai
